verses.text: Now, brothers and sisters, I want you to understand about the gifts of the Spirit.
You know that before you believed, you were led astray and carried away to worship idols that cannot speak.
So I want you to know that no one speaking by God's Spirit says, "Jesus is cursed." And no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different ways to serve, but we serve the same Lord.
There are different kinds of work, but the same God does all the work in all people.
The Spirit shows himself in each person for the good of everyone.
To one person the Spirit gives a message of wisdom. To another, the same Spirit gives a message of knowledge.
To another, the same Spirit gives faith. To another, the one Spirit gives gifts of healing.

To another he gives power to do miracles, and to another the gift of speaking God's message. To another he gives the ability to tell which spirits are from God. To another he gives the ability to speak in different kinds of languages, and to another the ability to explain what those languages mean.
All these are the work of one and the same Spirit. He gives them to each person as he chooses.
A body is one, even though it has many parts. All its many parts make up one body. It is the same with Christ.
For we were all baptised by one Spirit into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free. And we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
The body is not made up of one part, but of many.
If the foot said, "I am not a hand, so I am not part of the body," that would not stop it being part of the body.
And if the ear said, "I am not an eye, so I am not part of the body," that would not stop it being part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, how could it hear? If the whole body were an ear, how could it smell?
But God has put each part in the body just as he wanted.
If they were all one part, there would be no body.
As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I do not need you." And the head cannot say to the feet, "I do not need you."
In fact, the parts of the body that seem weaker are the ones we cannot do without.
The parts we think are less honourable, we treat with special honour. The private parts we cover with special care,
while the parts that can be seen need no special care. But God has put the body together and given more honour to the parts that lacked it.
So there should be no division in the body. Instead, all its parts should care for each other equally.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. If one part is honoured, every part is happy with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

In the church God has given first apostles, second prophets, third teachers. Then there are those who do miracles, those with gifts of healing, those who help others, those who lead, and those who speak in different kinds of languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all do miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in other languages? Do all explain what they mean?
But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the best way of all.
